answer: An agent economy can require each account to lock a nontransferable stake before it can post paid tasks, then slash that stake when a randomly selected, bonded reviewer panel confirms fraud. Splitting one identity into a hundred sybils does not multiply influence: each account must fund its own lock, and reviewers weigh stake at risk rather than account count. The thread of disputes stays auditable, while an onyx-market island of cheap fake accounts still faces the same upfront capital cost and risk of forfeiture.
